newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hebron Jews seize houses in Arab casbah.
newsitem.headline: Hebron Jews seize houses in Arab casbah.

text.p: Jewish settlers, angry at progress towards an Israeli government deal with Palestinians to hand over much of Hebron, took over two buildings in the town's Arab casbah early on Wednesday, witnesses said.

They said about 20 Jews broke into the houses only a day after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyanu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat made progress on a long-overdue Israeli handover of much of the West Bank town to Palestinian self-rule.
Israeli security forces began using force to try to remove some of the settlers, mainly women and children, while men conducted Jewish morning prayers in one of the houses, witnesses said.
Three right-wing members of parliament, including Deputy Education Minister Moshe Peled, turned out in solidarity with the settlers. Peled said he was not there on behalf of the Netanyahu government.

Under a 1995 peace deal, Israel is to give Palestinians control of 80 percent of Hebron, holy to both Jews and Moslems as the burial place of the biblical Abraham. The two leaders closed in on a deal during a summit on Tuesday.
The 400 settlers who live in the heart of the town of 100,000 Arabs fear the deal will endanger their security. Israel captured the town with the rest of the West Bank in the 1967 Middle East war.

"This morning Jews entered a number of buildings in Hebron. One house is called Magen Avot and it is a Jewish house into which the entry symbolises our drive to prevent the toppling of Jewish buildings by the PLO," settler spokesman Noam Arnon said.

"The second building is very close to the (Jewish) Avraham Avinu neighbourhood and in these buildings the PLO is carrying out millions of dollars of renovations with the intention of housing hundreds of released terrorists," he told reporters.

The Arab casbah is in the 20 percent of Hebron due to remain under Israeli occupation in the deal along with the Jewish enclaves. Netanyahu has vowed to protect the settlers in the flashpoint town holy to both Moslems and Jews.
